sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Setup
sections.what: Imports the state helper from React. The shown part of the file does not use it.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.

sections.name: ResearchSettings
sections.title: Research settings shape
sections.what: Describes the research settings: the focus, the number of sources per project, optional primary links, whether web search is on, and a Yard only switch that skips web research.
sections.why: Gives one agreed shape for these settings.
sections.watch_out: With Yard only on, a run may use only saved information, so results can be narrower.

sections.name: FOCUS
sections.title: Focus choices
sections.what: Lists the two focus choices, Cost and schedule and Delivery lessons, with their stored values.
sections.why: Gives readable names for each focus.
sections.watch_out: The stored focus value must match these entries exactly.

sections.name: DEPTH
sections.title: Depth choices
sections.what: Lists the three depth choices, Standard, Deep and Exhaustive, each with a number of sources per project.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets the visitor trade thoroughness for time.
sections.watch_out: A higher number means more reading, so runs take longer; the file does not say by how much.

sections.name: Pills
sections.title: Choice buttons for focus and depth
sections.what: Draws a row of mutually exclusive choice buttons, used for the research focus and the number of pages to try. The selected choice is highlighted and marked as selected for screen readers.
sections.why: Likely reason: one reusable control keeps the look and behaviour of these settings the same.
sections.watch_out: The test id for each button is built from the group name and value, so renaming a group changes the ids that tests rely on.

sections.name: ResearchOptions
sections.title: Research settings panel
sections.what: The settings a user chooses before a scan: use Yard data only, what to look for, how many pages to try per project, whether to search the web, and whether to add their own links for each project. Own links must start with http or https, and an invalid link is flagged in red. Turning on Yard-only hides every other research option.
sections.why: The header explains that every selected project is researched and that own links go through the same checks as other sources.
sections.watch_out: The red flag marks a bad link, but the code appears to save every link typed, including invalid ones, and unticking the own-links box does not clear links already saved (reason not stated in the code, so this is inferred from reading the handlers).

summary: Defines the research settings a visitor can choose before a run, with the focus choices and the depth choices.
purpose: Gives the research settings one shared shape and the fixed choices offered for focus and depth.
why: Likely reason: one definition of the settings keeps the form and the run working from the same shape.
how: Declares the settings shape: focus, number of sources per project, optional primary sources, optional web search, and a Yard only switch. Then lists the two focus choices and the three depth choices with their labels. The component that presents these choices is not included in this excerpt.
inputs: The file takes no input; the visitor's choices are made elsewhere.
outputs: The settings shape and the fixed option lists for a form to display.
risks: Changing a depth number changes how many sources each run reads, which affects time and cost. The file does not set limits on the other settings.
debug: If a choice is missing from the form, check the lists in this file. If a run reads more or fewer sources than expected, check the depth number. Yard only means web research is skipped.
